title: Housing-first referrals from hospital social work: who is housed, what follows, and what blocks referral
subtitle: Convergent mixed methods study to shape a hospital referral pathway
statement: Hospital social workers can refer inpatients experiencing homelessness directly to the city's housing-first programme, but referral rates vary between social workers, many referrals are declined as incomplete, and nobody knows how many referred patients are housed or how their hospital use changes. The hospital wants a referral pathway grounded in what happens to referred people and in what helps or blocks referral.
whoAffected: People experiencing homelessness admitted to the hospital, about 900 admissions a year; the inclusion health social work team; housing-first staff; emergency department and ward teams.
whatHurts: A referral that fails because of a missing document or a discharge before contact sends a person back to the street; repeated emergency visits and readmissions follow, and trust in services erodes further.
currentPractice: Referral at the discretion of each social worker with a free-text form; no shared contact after discharge; no follow-up of housing outcomes.
whyNow: 142 referrals in 2025 with unknown outcomes, an executive request for a pathway by September 2027, and ethics approval of the protocol outline.
constraints: Existing social work staff plus one peer researcher paid by the hour; hospital data from 2024 and 2025; tenancy outcomes only through a signed data-sharing agreement; a pathway proposal due to the hospital executive in September 2027.
patientCenteredGoal: People experiencing homelessness who are admitted to hospital leave with a referral that works and a home to go to as soon as possible.
summary: Problem framed for a convergent mixed methods study of hospital referrals to housing first.
